preconditions: event loop accepts uninstall and closes acknowledgement
outcomes: Notification is received, uninstall is accepted, acknowledgement closes, then Unsubscribe returns.
After verified acknowledgement closure, the owned call fails to return under the declared driver watchdog; scheduling starvation remains a separate uncertainty.
schedules.unknown: A two-second fixture watchdog is not an API latency contract or production liveness proof.

preconditions: eventLoop is already blocked sending on this exact unbuffered status channel
Unsubscribe is blocked sending uninstall to that same event loop
outcomes: Both sends wait: the event loop cannot accept uninstall, and Unsubscribe has not reached its draining loop. This conditional channel cycle does not prove actual RPC reachability.

An owned rescue receiver permits status send, event loop uninstall reception, acknowledgement closure and call return. Record this after the original observation, never as successful unassisted completion.
schedules.unknown: Absent a verified pair of blocked sends, timeout alone is unknown rather than a detected cycle.

preconditions: a finite additional notification is offered
outcomes: The post-registration loop receives/discards the extra status and returns only when acknowledgement closes.
Returning before the acknowledgement closes violates this proposed handshake observation, if the driver proves request identity and no previous once completion.
schedules.unknown: If no finite-drain or acknowledgement ordering receipt exists, do not infer which select case ran.

outcomes: The call stays pending while acknowledgement is withheld and can return after it closes.
A proven return before acknowledgement closure violates the proposed completion order.
schedules.unknown: Host starvation after acknowledgement is not automatically an implementation deadlock.

preconditions: two calls share the same fresh subscription object
outcomes: sync.Once executes one uninstall body; both calls complete after that body returns.
More than one uninstall request attributable to this exact object contradicts the single Once body; two distinct subscriptions do not satisfy this condition.
schedules.unknown: A call blocked behind the same unfinished Once is not a second independent failure family.

preconditions: head deadline distance is strictly below twice respTimeout
outcomes: The first near head causes Reset(dist) and immediate return, preserving both list elements.
Removing this near head as clockwarp conflicts with the verified strict comparison and supplied deadline.
schedules.unknown: A recorded Reset request does not prove real timer firing, and equality at twice respTimeout is outside this near precondition.

preconditions: two synthetic far deadlines at or above twice respTimeout
each errc has capacity for one result
outcomes: Original Remove clears the removed cursor; el.Next then ends the loop. One clockwarp is sent, the second matcher remains and Stop is requested. This is a source-supported synthetic observation, not a verified real-clock failure.
Both far matchers removed may describe a separately pinned cursor-fix candidate; it is not the outcome of the declared original source.
schedules.unknown: Synthetic far deadlines cannot establish wall-clock rollback reachability with monotonic timestamps.

preconditions: synthetic far head followed by near tail
head error channel accepts one result
outcomes: The original cursor stops after removing head, leaving the near tail without a new Reset request in this invocation.
A next-before-remove candidate can reach tail, but candidate identity and timer state must be recorded separately from original-source expectation.
schedules.unknown: Later outer-loop events may reset the timer; this bounded single invocation does not prove indefinite loss.

preconditions: explicitly select response or timeout branch
two matching/completed or expired matchers in known order
each result channel can accept a result
outcomes: In response branch, a true requestDone removes first and traversal ends; a second matching matcher is not visited in this invocation.
In timeout branch, removing first expired cursor ends traversal; next event behavior is a separate trace.
If callback requestDone is false, cursor is retained so traversal can continue to the second matcher.
schedules.unknown: A response callback's ok and requestDone are different values; matching is not identical to completion. These branches remain one proposed mechanism family.

preconditions: Anzeon configuration is nil selecting Origin loop
exit is not ready at that select
outcomes: commit sends work then resets timer and newTxs; eventual outer exit is a separate event.
An exit return would require a readiness change inconsistent with the stipulated select; inspect actual trace before assigning a fault.
schedules.unknown: No deterministic outer-loop termination bound follows from source or a fixture's watchdog.

outcomes: Only exit is ready in commit, so closure returns; timer.Reset/newTxs.Store below that select do not execute.
After closure return the outer select can process another ready event or exit; closure return alone does not prove worker leak or whole-function return.
schedules.unknown: Distinguish closure and goroutine/function return coordinates and counters.

preconditions: send and exit both ready at selection
outcomes: Sending work is a language-permitted ready-select choice; timer.Reset/newTxs.Store follow.
Selecting exit is also permitted; closure returns without send/reset.
Neither allowed branch is a product violation until cancellation linearization and accepted-work policy are independently defined.
schedules.unknown: Do not require a 50/50 frequency, priority for exit, or infer bug from a single ready-send choice.

preconditions: start/head events and exit are ready
outcomes: The outer exit branch returns the function and deferred timer/WaitGroup cleanup runs.
A ready event may be chosen first and invoke commit again; source gives no deterministic priority or count bound.
Finite observation without return alone establishes neither unbounded starvation nor a leak; record window and events.
schedules.unknown: Multiple outer-loop iterations remain correlated traces, not independent shutdown defects.

preconditions: broadcaster returns exactly one eligible peer
fresh hash absent from that peer cache
outcomes: Per-peer cache insertion precedes goroutine send; Gossip returns nil without collecting its result.
Gossip nil and SendWBFTConsensus nil do not prove network delivery or consensus acceptance.
schedules.unknown: Missing broadcaster/targets/peers yields no attempt and is outside this ready-peer precondition, not automatic send failure.

preconditions: first fake sender result is error
outcomes: Original code retains mark before error-producing asynchronous call; second same-peer/hash invocation skips it.
Whether suppression after an error violates product retry policy requires independent best-effort/cache-contract review; no defect is asserted.
schedules.unknown: Other routes, cache eviction or expiration may enable later delivery; no permanent/global loss conclusion.

preconditions: first sender is held by owned fake
release and join owned sender at cleanup
outcomes: The second call sees the existing mark and skips; mark denotes attempted scheduling, not completed delivery.
Parent nil is not the asynchronous sender result; ownership and result timestamps must remain separate.
schedules.unknown: A delayed fake sender is not observed network backpressure or a leak in a live deployment.

preconditions: a truly distinct hash or a peer cache without this hash
outcomes: The distinct cache key is inserted and a new asynchronous send is scheduled.
Global knownMessages insertion here is not used as the per-peer skip condition; distinct peer/hash policy must be evaluated locally.
schedules.unknown: Fresh cache does not imply independent family or prove eventual delivery.

preconditions: StateAt succeeds and reorg produces nonempty successfully reinjected adds
reorg subscriber is ready to receive insertFeed
outcomes: Send can finish, Reset eventually leaves and releases lock; Stats can then acquire it.
Stats waiting before Reset actually returns is compatible with the same mutex and is not itself a deadlock.
schedules.unknown: If reorg has no adds or StateAt fails, the stipulated send was not reached; do not count an easy return as a valid normal trial.

preconditions: Reset holds pool lock at insertFeed.Send with nonempty adds
sole subscriber waits on Stats before receiving
outcomes: Feed waits for subscriber while Stats waits for the lock held by Reset. Conditional cycle is source-supported, actual subscriber order remains unverified.
An owned receive or unsubscribe releases this Send dependency; record observation before rescue and join owned work afterwards.
schedules.unknown: Documented buffering/backpressure obligations may assign responsibility to caller; no operational defect or safety verdict.

preconditions: one subscribed channel has space for exactly this one event
outcomes: The event fits without waiting for receiver; Reset can return and Stats then consume lock before receive.
This one-event control proves no claim about full buffers, multiple subscribers, repeated events or all-load safety.
schedules.unknown: Free capacity must be captured at Send, not assumed from channel capacity at construction.

preconditions: Feed.Send is blocked solely on this slow subscriber
owned unsubscribe path is invoked for same subscription
other subscribers are absent or ready
outcomes: Feed removeSub case removes pending send; after Send and remaining Reset work, deferred pool unlock permits Stats.
Subscription removal is not the pool unlock itself and imposes no immediate end-to-end timing bound.
schedules.unknown: If another subscriber still blocks Send, lack of return does not refute removal of this subscriber.
